# Phase 0 decisions and open questions

Where the spec was silent or inconsistent, phase 0 chose as follows. Change any of these through `requests/` with a reason.

## Decisions

- **Go 1.27.2.** The current stable release on 2026-10-13, pinned with the `toolchain` directive.
- **Node 24 LTS and pnpm 11.28.2.** Node 20 reached end of life in April 2026 and Vite 8 needs 20.19 or later. pnpm 12 does not run through the installed corepack, so the UI pins the latest pnpm 11. TypeScript stays on 5.9 because `openapi-typescript` 7 needs TypeScript 5.
- **Column `commit_sha`, not `commit`.** `COMMIT` is a keyword in SQLite, so the tables in 02 that have a `commit` column (`tree_entries`, `dependencies`, `metadata`, `scan_results`, `dataset_splits`, `dataset_stats`) use `commit_sha`. `dataset_stats.column` is `column_name` for the same reason.
- **Column `tokens.scope`, not `scopes`.** A Token has one scope level (05-auth.md: admin includes write, write includes read).
- **Extra tables.** `ollama_blobs` (08), plus `ollama_nonces`, `invites`, `password_resets`, `email_changes` (added in migration `0003`, see "Self-set emails wait for confirmation" below), `login_attempts`, `oidc_states`, `oauth_device_codes` and `rate_limit_leases`, because 05, 06 and 08 need state that must be shared across replicas.
- **Extra configuration keys.** `server.data_dir` (where `secrets.yaml` and the SQLite lock live), `server.shutdown_timeout` and `server.timezone` (named in 02 and 11), `repos.restore_window` (REPO-5), `hfapi.default_namespace` (single-segment redirects), `upstreams.<id>.namespace_prefix` and `viewer_url` (06, 14), `pull.pull_through.min_role` (06), `viewer.*` (14) and `telemetry.environment`, `prometheus_listen`, `log_format`, `log_level` (11). `git.cache_dir`, `git.cache_size` and `git.timeout` follow the YAML in 02, not the `server.git_*` names in 04.
- **Telemetry defaults.** 02 shows `otlp` and 11 says a quickstart makes no connections. Both hold: the default is `otlp`, which exports only when an OTLP endpoint variable is set.
- **Flags.** Every key can be set with `--set key=value`; `--role`, `--listen` and `--public-url` are shortcuts.
- **Reserved names.** `new-dataset` is reserved as well as the list in 02, because it is a UI route at the root.
- **Default `.gitattributes`.** Copied from Repos created on huggingface.co on 2026-10-13: one file for models and one for datasets, which the Hub gives extra media rules.
- **Native API.** The Discover endpoints take the Repo type in the path (`/discover/{type}`), so datasets use the same shape as models (DATA-7). `GET /repos/datasets/{ns}/{name}/configs` gives Configs, Splits and conversion status for the Viewer tab, owned by W10.
- **Phase 0 server wiring.** `cmd/hangar` serves the real health checks, the embedded UI and the generated native API router (answering 501 until handlers exist). The other protocols are stand-ins from `internal/httpx/httpxtest`, the Blob store is in memory, and every request is anonymous. Phase 2 replaces them.
- **Bootstrap admin username `hangar-admin`.** Decided by the integration lead on 2026-10-13. The default `security.bootstrap_admin.username` is `hangar-admin`, not `admin`, because `admin` is a reserved Namespace name and `/admin` is a UI route, so the bootstrap admin's personal Namespace page and Repos would be shadowed by the admin UI. Config validation refuses reserved names for this key. W5 implements the bootstrap step.
- **Owners of native API endpoints the build plan left unowned.** Decided by the integration lead on 2026-10-13: `/jobs` and `/admin/system` belong to W1, `/search` and `/namespaces` to W2, and `/me/device` and `/admin/settings` to W5.
- **Packages outside the layout in 02.** Decided by the integration lead on 2026-10-13: the integration lead owns `internal/contracttest`, `internal/secrets`, `internal/pins` and `internal/httpx/httpxtest`. Phase 2 deleted `internal/pins` once every pinned module was imported by real code.
- **A write Token administers Repos through the Hub API only.** Decided by James on 2026-10-17 ("Hub actions only"), narrowing commit `54e5307`, which had let a write Token do every Repo admin action (bellatrix finding 7). huggingface.co has read and write Tokens only and takes the rest from the user's Role ("according to the token permission (read/write) and organization membership (read/write/admin)", hub-docs `security-tokens.md`), so `delete_repo`, `move_repo` and `update_repo_settings` work there with a write Token. Hangar allows exactly that and no more: a write Token may delete a Repo, change its visibility or gating, and rename it within its Namespace, only through `DELETE /api/repos/delete`, `PUT /api/{type}s/{repo}/settings` and a same-Namespace `POST /api/repos/move`, and only when the user's Role on the Repo is `admin` (the `hub_admin` action in `internal/auth`). Transfers to another Namespace, webhooks, collaborators, access-request decisions and every native API admin action need the `admin` scope, as do managing an Organisation's Members and the Instance. Recorded in [05](../spec/05-auth.md) "Permission rules".

## Decisions from Phase 3 security

- **Browser credentials refuse cross-origin changes; Basic is for git only.** Decided by the phase 3 authz agent on 2026-10-17, from phase 3 security input 5. A state-changing request that carries the session cookie or HTTP Basic credentials is refused with 403 when `Sec-Fetch-Site` marks it as cross-origin, or, without `Sec-Fetch-Site`, when its `Origin` names neither the request's host nor `server.public_url` (Go's `net/http.CrossOriginProtection`, with `public_url` as a trusted origin). Sign-in calls get the same check without a cookie. A Token as an HTTP Basic password is accepted only on git and git-lfs routes, as [05](../spec/05-auth.md) already listed; other API routes answer 401, and the static UI and health routes ignore Basic credentials. The check compares `Origin` with the request's host as well as `public_url`, not with `public_url` alone, so the UI keeps working when a browser reaches Hangar by another name; a same-origin request cannot be forged, so this adds no exposure. Recorded in 05 "Sessions" and "Tokens".

## Decisions from the Phase 3 input review

Made by the Phase 3 security agent for untrusted input, on 2026-10-17, under the build plan's instruction to decide the default network policy with the spec. Each can be changed through `requests/` with a reason.

- **Outbound network policy.** Hangar never connects to reserved addresses (link-local, which includes the cloud metadata service, other metadata services, unspecified, broadcast and multicast), for Upstreams or webhooks, whatever the settings. An Upstream's own host may be anywhere else, so LAN Upstreams keep working; a redirect to another host may reach a private address only when the Upstream's own host is private. Webhooks keep `webhooks.allow_private_targets` (default on). Checks apply to the address dialled, after DNS. Recorded in [06](../spec/06-upstreams-and-pulls.md) "Network policy" and [10](../spec/10-native-api.md).
- **Git input limits.** Pushed and fetched packs and their Commits are held to the limits in [04](../spec/04-git.md) "Pack and tree limits": objects and deltas up to the larger of `git.max_blob_size` and 64 MiB, 2,000,000 objects per pushed pack, four times `git.max_pack_size` (at least 1 GiB) unpacked, 10,000 ref updates per push, 1,000,000 paths per Commit, 4,096-byte paths, 100,000 refs read from an Upstream. They are constants rather than configuration keys: each is far above what a real model or dataset Repo needs (02 targets 100,000 files per Repo), and a key can be added if one proves too low.
- **Names a Repo cannot hold.** Pushes, Pulls and Commits refuse the names git's fsck refuses (`.`, `..`, `.git` in any case and its NTFS and HFS+ spellings, names with `/`) and names with a backslash, which the commit API already refused. A Mirror of an Upstream Repo with such a name fails to Pull with a message naming it, rather than holding a file no Hub API path can reach and that extracts outside a client's folder on Windows.
- **Symbolic links in uploaded folders.** `hangar push` and `hangar import` follow a link only into the folder, into the Repo's cache folder for a Hugging Face cache snapshot, or to a Hugging Face cache blob; other links are skipped and named. huggingface_hub's `upload_folder` follows every link, so a folder with a link out of it uploads less with Hangar's CLI than with `huggingface_hub`.
## Decisions from the Phase 3 performance review

- **Password hashing is bounded per process.** Decided by the Phase 3 performance agent on 2026-10-17 from a load test: 40 parallel failed sign-ins took a 1 GiB web replica to its limit and got another OOM-killed, because every argon2id check holds 64 MiB and nothing limited how many ran at once. At most two hashes or checks run at once per process (one for each two CPUs, so one on a 2 CPU replica); the rest wait and give up when their request ends. The argon2id parameters in [05](../spec/05-auth.md) are unchanged. A flood of sign-ins now queues instead of exhausting memory, so it can still slow sign-in for everyone on that replica; rate limiting sign-in by IP at the proxy remains the operator's tool for that.
- **Load test scenarios.** Decided by the Phase 3 performance agent on 2026-10-17. `upload.js` commits each client's file to its own Repo, because concurrent Commits to one branch without a parent Commit may get 409 once their bounded retries run out ([04](../spec/04-git.md) "Server-side Commits"), and the scenario measures upload memory, not ref contention. `download.js` and `viewer_rows.js` cover the download memory and throughput targets in [02](../spec/02-architecture.md) and the `/rows` target in [14](../spec/14-datasets.md). [13](../spec/13-testing.md) lists them. Results are in `docs/benchmarks.md`.
## Decisions from the Phase 3 gaps

- **`storage.s3.startup_wait`.** Decided by the phase 3 gaps agent on 2026-10-17, from the round 9 kind run where Hangar exited because MinIO started late. A server or worker now listens before it opens the Blob store, answers `/healthz` while it waits, keeps `/readyz` at 503 with the reason, and retries an S3 store that does not answer for up to `storage.s3.startup_wait` (default `5m`, the same as the chart's `migrations.waitForDatabase`; `0` keeps the old fail-at-once behaviour) before it exits. Every S3 error is retried, as `--wait-for-database` retries every Postgres error, because a bucket or credentials that a GitOps install creates next to Hangar may appear late too. The filesystem backend is not retried. Documented in [02](../spec/02-architecture.md) and [Storage](../operate/storage.md).

## Decisions from the bellatrix preview

James used a preview on his home cluster on 2026-10-16 and decided the following that day.

- **Release on hold.** Decided by James on 2026-10-16. Nothing is published until James says go: no public repository, no push to GitHub, no tags, no release-please run or release pull request, no images on GHCR, no GitHub Pages site and no Helm chart in a registry. Agents and the integration lead carry the work up to and including the release dry run (`make release-rehearsal` and a GoReleaser snapshot, which publish nothing), then stop and ask James. Phase 4 in [15](../spec/15-build-plan.md) waits for his go.
- **Taxiway teal accent.** Decided by James on 2026-10-16. The UI's accent changes from amber to Taxiway teal: light `--hg-accent` `#0b6e64`, `--hg-accent-fill` `#0b7a6e`, `--hg-accent-ink` `#ffffff`, `--hg-accent-soft` `#dff3ef`; dark `#5fd4c2`, `#2bb3a0`, `#021a17`, `#12332e`. Warnings stay amber, so the accent no longer looks like a warning. The amber colour tokens are gone, components use only the semantic tokens, and the logo's bay line, the favicon, the docs icon and the docs site accent follow. The palette is in [09](../spec/09-web-ui.md) "Visual direction".
- **Models and Datasets are separate sections.** Decided by James on 2026-10-16. The top bar has **Models** (`/models`) and **Datasets** (`/datasets`) in place of the mixed **Arsenal** list. Each has its own list, filters, empty state and **New model** or **New dataset** button, and no list mixes the two types: the search palette groups results by type and Namespace pages list models and datasets separately. `/` shows the Models list to signed-in users. `/arsenal` stays as a redirect so old links work: to `/datasets` for `type=datasets`, to `/models` otherwise, with the other query parameters kept. Collections stay the way to group a project's models and datasets. "Arsenal" still names everything in an Instance (`CONTEXT.md`).
- **Optional links between models and datasets.** Decided by James on 2026-10-16. A model's **Settings** tab has a **Datasets used** picker that commits the Model card's `datasets` metadata as the Hub stores it, a list of dataset IDs, keeping the card's other keys and text. The model's sidebar lists them under **Datasets used** and each dataset's sidebar lists the models under **Used by**, from the Dependencies Hangar already resolves from the card. A dataset with no links is normal.
- **Datasets hold any files.** Decided by James on 2026-10-16. A dataset of files the Dataset Viewer cannot read, such as sample data for another project, reads as a normal dataset: the Viewer tab says there is nothing to preview and why, and links to the files; **Use this dataset** offers only the download snippets.
- **Equal-height cards.** Decided by James on 2026-10-16. Repo cards in a grid row are the same height, with the stats row at the bottom, and show three quant chips, then a **+N** chip whose accessible name and tooltip list the rest.

## Decisions from the Phase 3 security review of the scanner

Made by the phase 3 scan agent on 2026-10-17 from the security inputs for `scan.block_unsafe_downloads` (items 1, 2 and 6). Details are in [the handoff](handoffs/p3-scan.md) and [07](../spec/07-indexing-and-scanning.md).

- **Content decides how a file is read.** A `.bin` file is no longer skipped because an `.xml` file of the same name exists; data that fails at its first opcode is not a pickle and is safe.
- **More names are scanned.** `.npz`, and the pickle, joblib and NumPy names with a compression or archive suffix (`.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.lzma`, `.z`, `.zst`, `.lz4`, `.zip`, `.tar`), because `joblib.load`, `numpy.load` and `pandas.read_pickle` load them.
- **Partial results fail closed.** A scan that could not follow a file to where every loader stops records `partial`, and the Gate refuses such files that can run code, with `accept_risk=1` still working on the Hub API. A parse error where every loader also stops does not block. Results of scanner version 1 with an error count as partial until the rescan.
- **joblib is read as joblib reads it.** The scanner follows `NumpyArrayWrapper` array data and frames as `joblib.load` does, as well as the `pickle.load` reading.
- **Objects are decided from every Commit that holds them**, not only ref tips and Commits with unsafe files.
- **git clone and fetch are gated.** git-upload-pack is refused while a reachable Commit holds a refused file stored in git rather than LFS, or the history is too long to check.
- **Scanner version 2.** The rescan of every ref tip runs when workers start.

## Decisions from the Phase 3 docs walk-through

Made on 2026-10-17 where a page under `docs/get-started` or `docs/guides` and the product disagreed; the log is in [docs-walkthrough.md](docs-walkthrough.md).

- **Discover opens a Repo by ID.** huggingface.co search leaves some organisations out, such as `hf-internal-testing`, so the first-pull guide's Repo could not be found by searching. A Discover search of the form `namespace/name` also offers **Open** for that Repo ([09](../spec/09-web-ui.md)).
- **A gating update keeps the keys it does not send.** `PATCH /repos/{type}/{ns}/{name}` with `gating` changes only the gating keys in the body, so saving the mode in the UI no longer clears request form fields set through the API.
- **`hangar push --branch` creates a missing branch** from the default branch, as `hf upload --revision` does.
- **An anonymous 401 from an Upstream is not found.** huggingface.co answers an anonymous request for a Repo that does not exist with a bare 401; with no credentials sent, Hangar reads it as not found, as `huggingface_hub` does, instead of saying the Upstream rejected the user's credentials.

## Phase 3 decisions by James (2026-10-18), access, Commits and Ollama

James answered three of the open questions on 2026-10-18.

- **Namespace profiles need sign-in while `anonymous_read` is off.** User and Organisation profiles, Organisation member lists, a user's likes (`GET /api/users/{user}/likes`), Namespace results in search and public Collections now follow `security.anonymous_read`: open to anyone while it is on, as on the Hub, and for signed-in callers only while it is off. Anonymous callers then get 401, as for a public Repo on the same Instance, from a check made before any lookup, so the answer does not reveal whether a Namespace or Member exists; search leaves users and Organisations out and Collection lists leave public Collections out, as Repo lists leave Repos out. Public Collections are included because a Namespace page lists them and they name the Namespace; they answer 404 to anonymous callers, as a private Collection does. No client flow changes: `huggingface_hub` does not call these endpoints anonymously, and the UI's Namespace page asks a signed-out visitor to sign in instead of loading the rest of the page. Recorded in [05](../spec/05-auth.md) "Permission rules", [09](../spec/09-web-ui.md) and [10](../spec/10-native-api.md); the route matrix has a `profile` rule for these routes.
- **Concurrent server-side Commits retry with jittered backoff.** A Commit without `parent_commit` that loses the compare-and-swap to another Commit on the same branch now waits a random time before it retries on the new tip ("full jitter" exponential backoff: up to `min(2 s, base × 2^(n-1))` before retry `n`, where `base` is the longer of 20 ms and the failed attempt's own time), and the bound rises from 3 retries to 7. The phase 3 performance review saw four concurrent Commits to one branch get 409 with 3 immediate retries; eight concurrent Commits to one branch now all land on SQLite and Postgres (`TestConcurrentCommitsToOneBranch`), where the old code failed every run on SQLite. The bound stays, so a Commit still gets 409 under sustained contention, and a Commit with a `parent_commit` that no longer matches still fails at once with 412, as the Hub API contract requires. A per-ref lock was not chosen because it holds a database lock across a pack upload to the Blob store. Recorded in [04](../spec/04-git.md) "Server-side Commits".
- **`hangar ollama install` checks the quant first; the registry keeps its 404.** The Ollama registry still answers a quant that is not in the Arsenal with 404 `MANIFEST_UNKNOWN` and a message naming the Pull, as [08](../spec/08-local-tools.md) says, although Ollama 0.31 shows only `file does not exist`. Before it runs `ollama pull`, `hangar ollama install` now asks the Instance for the quant the registry would serve for the tag (`latest` without one: `Q4_K_M` or the closest quant), matched the way the registry matches it, and checks that its files and its projector are in the Arsenal. If not, it says so, prints `hangar pull <repo>:<quant> --server-only`, and asks whether to run it, as it asks about the Ollama key; `--pull` runs it without asking, and any other answer exits 3 without running Ollama. A Repo that is not in the Arsenal at all names the quant the Upstream would give. A signed-out CLI that cannot read the Repo skips the check, because Ollama signs its own requests. Recorded in [08](../spec/08-local-tools.md) and the [Ollama guide](../guides/ollama.md).

## Phase 3 decisions by James (2026-10-18), scan and storage

- **The download gate's level is a setting.** Decided by James on 2026-10-18 ("make it a setting"), from the open question the phase 3 scan review raised. The Instance setting `scan.block_level` (`scan_block_level` in the native API, **What to block** under **Admin**, **Settings**) is `unsafe` or `suspicious`, default `unsafe`, which keeps the behaviour before the decision. With `scan.block_unsafe_downloads` on, `unsafe` refuses files the scan marked unsafe; `suspicious` also refuses files with imports on neither the allow nor the deny list, which matches what `torch.load(weights_only=True)` refuses. `accept_risk=1` overrides both on the Hub API and in the web UI. Every route that serves file bytes applies it through `scan.Gate`: Hub API resolve, git-lfs batch and signed object links, the Ollama registry, Pull-through links, zip exports and git clone and fetch (Hangar offers no Xet downloads). The web UI asks before it downloads a suspicious pickle and sends `accept_risk=1`. Tests: `TestGateBlockLevel` (`internal/scan`), `TestSuspiciousDownloadsFollowTheBlockLevel` (`cmd/hangar`, every route at both levels), `TestSettings` (`internal/auth`), `TestAdminEndpoints` (`internal/api`). Recorded in [07](../spec/07-indexing-and-scanning.md) "Where results show" and [Security hardening](../operate/security.md#choose-what-to-block).
- **LFS and Xet objects are checked at Commit.** Decided by James on 2026-10-18 ("check at Commit"), from the open question the phase 3 authz review raised. LFS objects stay stored once per Instance (UP-6), but a Commit, a git push, a `create_pr=1` commit or a native API commit may add a pointer to an object only when its author uploaded the bytes, through any upload path, or can read (`read_files`) a Repo that holds it, the target Repo included. Uploaders are recorded in the new table `lfs_uploaders` (migration `0002`); objects stored before it have none and stay usable through the Repos that hold them. Other pointers are refused with the error for an object that was never uploaded. The git-lfs batch, the native upload plan and verify answer such an object as missing, so huggingface_hub and git-lfs upload the bytes and succeed; the upload is checked and discarded, storing no second copy. Xet records the token's User when a shard rebuilds the file, no longer gives a stored object's size in errors, and verifies a xorb it already has before it answers `was_inserted: false`. No MUST in the contract changes: an object without `actions` still means "already present" (§7.6), and an unknown `lfsFile` still fails with 4xx (§7.7). Pulls into a Mirror are not checked, because an admin chooses every Upstream; this and the other residual risks are in the [threat model](../security/threat-model.md#lfs-object-references). Tests: `TestLFSObjectsOfPrivateReposCannotBeReferenced` (`cmd/hangar`), `TestCommitsReferenceOnlyObjectsTheActorUploadedOrCanRead` and `TestUploadsOfStoredObjectsProveTheBytes` (`internal/repo`), `TestLFSBatchAsksForObjectsTheCallerCannotUse` (`internal/gitserver`), `TestCommitsCannotReferenceObjectsOfPrivateRepos` (`internal/hfapi`), `TestXetUploadsRecordUploadersAndRevealNothing` (`internal/xet`), and the compat cases in `compat/git`, `compat/hf` and `compat/xet`. Recorded in [04](../spec/04-git.md) "Who may reference an LFS object", [03](../spec/03-hf-api.md) "Shard handling and reassembly", [02](../spec/02-architecture.md) and UP-6 in [01](../spec/01-product.md).

## Phase 3 decisions by James (2026-10-18), self-service accounts

- **Users change their own profile and password.** Decided by James on 2026-10-18, closing W8 8, which had left password changes to admin reset links. `PATCH /me` changes the signed-in user's display name through the admin user editor's code (`UserStore.Update`), so the checks and errors are the same (at most 100 bytes), and asks for a new email with the editor's checks: a valid address, and 409 `Already exists: the email address is already used.` for an email another User has, in any case. The email takes effect only once confirmed (next item). `POST /me/password` takes `current_password` and `new_password`. The rules below were chosen by the W8 8 agent under that decision, from [05](../spec/05-auth.md):
  - **Session only for passwords.** Every Token, whatever its scope, gets 403, because a leaked Token must not be able to lock its owner out; this follows 05's rule that linking a provider and approving a device need a UI session. The route matrix rule is `session_only`.
  - **A `write` Token may change the profile.** 05 gives every other `/me` change (Tokens, Ollama keys, Upstream tokens, sessions) to `write` Tokens, and a display name or email is no more sensitive: Hangar never sends mail and never links accounts by email automatically. A `read` Token gets 403. The route matrix rule is `signed_in_write`.
  - **Wrong current passwords use the sign-in throttle.** They count against the same per-username and per-IP keys as failed sign-ins, and a locked key answers 429 with `Retry-After`, so the form is no faster to guess through than sign-in. Wrong current passwords answer 403, not 401, with an error on `/current_password`, so clients do not read them as an ended session. A weak new password answers 422 with an error on `/new_password`.
  - **Other sessions end; Tokens stay.** Success deletes every session of the user except the current one, as a reset deletes them all, and resets the username's throttle. Tokens are separate credentials the user manages under **Settings**, **Tokens**, and ending them would break automation without being asked; [Security hardening](../operate/security.md) tells users to revoke them when they think their account was used.
  - **Audit events.** `user.password_changed` (with the number of sessions ended), `user.password_change_failed` (with the reason: `wrong_password`, `weak_password`, `throttled` or `no_password`) and `user.profile_changed` (with the names of the fields that changed, not their values).
  - **OIDC users.** 05 maps display name and email from the claims only when OIDC creates a User, and re-evaluates only admin groups and Organisation mappings at each login, so the provider does not own those fields after that: OIDC users may change them with `PATCH /me`, and later logins do not overwrite them. A User without a Hangar password, as OIDC creates them, gets 403 from `POST /me/password` telling them to change it with their provider; a local User who linked a provider keeps their password and may change it. `Me` gains `has_password` so the UI can tell the two apart.
  - **Self-set emails wait for confirmation; only verified emails match.** From the security review of 2026-10-18: an address a user typed could squat someone else's, blocking their OIDC first sign-in. An email a user sets for themselves, with `PATCH /me` or when registering (open registration, or an invite that names no email), is stored as pending in the new table `email_changes` (migration `0003`), outside `users.email` and its unique index, so it blocks no sign-in, invite or other user's change. Hangar has no mail, and reset links already work by an admin creating and sending them, so confirmation follows that: an admin creates a single-use link (`POST /admin/users/{id}/email-link`, **Email link** under **Admin**, **Users**; 72 hours; a new link replaces the last) and sends it to the address, and confirming it on the page it opens (`POST /auth/email/{code}`, which asks before it confirms, so a mail scanner opening the link changes nothing) makes it the verified email, or answers 409 if another User took the address meanwhile. Used, expired and replaced links answer 404. From a second security review the same day, the admin's request names the pending email the admin saw (the UI sends the address in the row), and the link is bound to it by an update with `AND email = ?` in one transaction, so a change the user makes between the admin looking and approving gives 409 instead of a link for another address; the response names the bound address, and the UI shows that one. A new pending email deletes the row, which ends any earlier link. OIDC first sign-in now refuses with "link the provider" only for a verified email; an unverified one is left alone and the new User gets no email. Emails an admin sets (creating a User, the admin editor, an invite's email) and the bootstrap admin's are verified at once, because the admin vouches for them; the admin editor's change also replaces a pending one. Migration `0003` marks every stored email verified, so existing admin-set emails keep matching; before it, admin-set emails were stored unverified, and the only Instance with data is the preview. `Me` and `AdminUser` gain `pending_email`; the audit action `user.email_confirmation` records links created and used.
  - **No CLI command.** The `hangar` CLI has no account or profile command group, and it authenticates with Tokens, which cannot change passwords, so there is no `hangar account password`.

  The UI's **Settings**, **Profile** page edits the display name and email and changes the password (current, new, confirm), and the first sign-in guide now points there instead of to a reset link. Tests: `TestChangePassword`, `TestUpdateProfile`, `TestSelfSetEmailsNeedConfirmation`, `TestRegistrationEmailsNeedConfirmation` (`internal/auth`), `TestUpdateMe`, `TestChangeMyPassword`, `TestChangeMyPasswordIsThrottled`, `TestEveryW5ActionIsAudited` (`internal/api`), `TestSelfServiceAccountOnTheFullServer`, `TestRouteAuthorisationMatrix` (`cmd/hangar`), the mock Playwright flows under "account" (`ui/e2e/flows.spec.ts`) and the real-Instance flow "changes the display name, email and password on the Profile page" (`ui/e2e-real/flows.spec.ts`). Recorded in [05](../spec/05-auth.md), [09](../spec/09-web-ui.md), [10](../spec/10-native-api.md) and the [threat model](../security/threat-model.md).

## Website and name, decided by James (2026-10-18)

- **The website is `https://hangar.page/`.** James chose the domain and buys it himself. The documentation stays on GitHub Pages, published by mike from the `gh-pages` branch, with `hangar.page` as the custom domain in place of `https://jamesagarside.github.io/hangar/`. `site_url` in `mkdocs.yml` is `https://hangar.page/`, so canonical URLs and sitemaps have no `/hangar/` prefix; mike adds the version directory. Only the site root redirects (to `latest`), so links to a page from outside the site use `https://hangar.page/latest/<page>/`. GitHub Pages reads the domain from a `CNAME` at the root of `gh-pages`, which mike leaves alone; `scripts/docs-cname.sh` runs after every publish in `docs.yml` and `release.yml` and commits one if it is missing. The DNS, domain verification and HTTPS steps are James's, in the v1.0.0 checklist in [12](../spec/12-packaging-and-release.md#release-v100-checklist). Later the same day James moved the hosting to Cloudflare, and `scripts/docs-cname.sh` went with GitHub Pages; see the next section.
- **The name stays plain "Hangar".** A preliminary trademark search rated the name medium risk. James keeps it for a free, non-commercial, source-available release; a commercial offering would need a fuller clearance first.
- **No PyPI or npm package named `hangar`.** Both names are taken. Hangar ships no Python or npm package (the binary, the image, the Helm chart and the Homebrew cask are the only artefacts), so neither is needed.

## Docs and demo on Cloudflare, decided by James (2026-10-18)

James decided to host Hangar's websites on Cloudflare instead of GitHub Pages ("keep it all on Cloudflare"): the docs at `https://hangar.page/`, and a demo of the web UI on the mock API at `https://demo.hangar.page/`, on the free plan. Recorded in [12](../spec/12-packaging-and-release.md), "Documentation site", "Demo" and the v1.0.0 checklist.

- **The docs are a Cloudflare Pages project that serves the `gh-pages` branch as it is.** Pages' Git integration can deploy a branch with no build command, so mike keeps publishing versions to `gh-pages` as before (`/dev/`, `/1.0/`, `/latest/`, and mike's root redirect), and Cloudflare deploys each push through its GitHub app. This needs no Cloudflare secret in GitHub, which a `wrangler pages deploy` or Workers static assets step in `docs.yml` and `release.yml` would need (an API token with Pages edit access), and it keeps the workflows as they were. The cost is a Cloudflare build for every push to `gh-pages`, well inside the free plan's 500 a month, and one manual setup in the dashboard. `scripts/docs-cname.sh` and the GitHub Pages DNS, domain verification and HTTPS steps are gone. `scripts/docs-root-files.sh` takes its place in both workflows and copies `deploy/cloudflare/docs-root/` (`_headers`, `_redirects`, a root `404.html`) to the root of `gh-pages`, which mike leaves alone.
- **Security headers for the docs.** `_headers` sends the Go server's headers and a Content Security Policy like its one, with `'unsafe-inline'` scripts and styles, Google Fonts, `api.github.com` and `cdn.jsdelivr.net` (Redoc) allowed, because Material's inline scripts change with each page's depth, so hashes would break on every Material upgrade. Checked with `wrangler pages dev` on a mike layout: no CSP violations on the home page, a guide, the native API page (Redoc renders), search and the version selector. The site has no user content or forms. HSTS needs no header, because `.page` is on the browsers' preload list.
- **Unversioned paths redirect to `latest`.** MkDocs builds each version's `404.html` with links from the site root, and Pages serves the nearest `404.html` for a missing page, so `_redirects` sends `/get-started/` and the other sections to `/latest/` and serves `/assets/` and `/search/` from `latest`. A test checks that every top-level section of `docs/` has a rule.
- **The demo is a Cloudflare Worker with static assets, deployed by Workers Builds from the `demo` branch.** The Worker runs the same mock as `vite preview`: `ui/mock/core.ts` now has no transport, `ui/mock/server.ts` adapts it to Node for Vite and `ui/mock/fetch.ts` to the Fetch API for the Worker. The OpenAPI validators are compiled ahead of time, because Workers cannot compile code at run time. `release.yml` moves `demo` to each release tag, so the demo matches `/latest/`, and Workers Builds runs `make demo` and `make demo-deploy` with its own token, so GitHub holds no Cloudflare credentials for either site. A workflow that runs `wrangler deploy` with a `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` secret would have tested the same `make` targets in GitHub Actions, at the cost of a secret.
- **The demo keeps nothing and cannot host files.** Visitors start signed in as `ada`, each with a copy of the fixtures in the isolate's memory, keyed by a session cookie. State resets when Cloudflare recycles the isolate, after an hour unused, or when the isolate drops the least recently used sessions to stay under 64 MiB. Request bodies over 1 MiB get 413 before the mock reads them, a session gets 413 for writes once it has sent 8 MiB, and upload parts are counted and dropped. Every response has `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, and pages get the Go server's CSP with a fresh nonce. A new session costs about 0.4 ms and a warm API request under 0.3 ms in Node, inside the free plan's 10 ms of CPU time per request; this was measured in Node, not on Cloudflare.
- **No open redirect and no shared state.** Found in review on 2026-10-18. The mock's OIDC sign-in sent visitors to any `redirect` value, which on a public domain is an open redirect for phishing; it now follows only paths on the demo, with the rules of `internal/auth.SafeRedirect` plus a same-origin check, and the UI's `safeRedirect` also refuses `/\` and control characters as the Go server does. The Go server already had the check (`SafeRedirect` in `internal/auth/oidc.go`, applied when the sign-in starts and at the callback). State was already per visitor, so one visitor cannot sign another out or plant content others see; `ui/mock/fetch.test.ts` and `ui/e2e-demo` now test both, and the export file name is kept free of quotes and line breaks.
- **The banner is a build flag.** `VITE_HANGAR_DEMO=1` adds "This is a demo with sample data. Nothing you do here is saved." and a link to the docs, and builds into `ui/demo/dist`; the embedded build in `internal/web/dist` has neither. `wrangler` 4.147.0 runs through `pnpm dlx`, pinned in the `Makefile`, so the UI's dependencies do not grow.
